> commands in your workspace can drive the wallet.

---

### Agent Frameworks

OpenClaw and Hermes are general-purpose personal assistants rather than coding tools. They install
their own runtime, connect to a model provider of your choice, and can take instructions from a
messaging app — useful if you want to check your wallet from your phone.

<Tabs defaultValue="openclaw" className="w-full">
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value="openclaw">OpenClaw</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="hermes">Hermes</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>

  <TabsContent value="openclaw">

**1. Install**

```bash
curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash
```

On Windows, run this in PowerShell instead:

```powershell
iwr -useb https://openclaw.ai/install.ps1 | iex
```

The installer provisions a supported Node.js runtime for you. If you manage Node yourself, install
the package directly with `npm install -g openclaw@latest --allow-scripts=openclaw`.

**2. Run onboarding**

The installer starts the setup wizard automatically. It walks you through choosing a model provider
and, optionally, a chat channel to control the assistant from. If you installed via npm, start it
manually:

```bash
openclaw onboard --install-daemon
```

**3. Install the Skills**

```bash
npx skills add binance/binance-skills-hub/skills/binance-web3/binance-agentic-wallet
```

Then continue with [Sign In](./install#step-3-sign-in). Full documentation:
[docs.openclaw.ai](https://docs.openclaw.ai/install).

  </TabsContent>

  <TabsContent value="hermes">

**1. Install**

```bash
curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash
```

On Windows, run this in PowerShell instead:

```powershell
iex (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1)
```

The installer handles Python, Node.js and the rest of its dependencies itself — nothing to prepare
in advance.

**2. Configure and start**

Reload your shell, then run the setup wizard to pick a model provider:

```bash
hermes setup
```

`hermes` starts an interactive session; `hermes gateway` starts the messaging gateway if you want to
drive it from Telegram or Discord.

**3. Install the Skills**

```bash
npx skills add binance/binance-skills-hub/skills/binance-web3/binance-agentic-wallet
```

Then continue with [Sign In](./install#step-3-sign-in). Full documentation:
[hermes-agent.nousresearch.com](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/).

  </TabsContent>
</Tabs>

---

## Security Baseline for Any Setup

An Agent with wallet access is a high-value target. Regardless of which client you chose:

- **Keep model API keys out of shared machines and repositories.** Use environment variables or your
  framework's credential store, never a committed file.
- **Set your wallet rules before the first trade.** Daily limit, tradable token scope, and high-risk
  transaction handling are configured in the Binance App and enforced at the API level — the Agent
  can read them but cannot change them.
- **Tighten the limit for anything unattended.** If your Agent can act while you are not watching —
  a scheduled task, a chat-driven assistant — it should not be able to move your whole balance.
- **Sign out when you are done**, especially on shared or temporary environments. One instruction —
  "Sign out" — revokes the session.

---

## Verify the Setup

Ask your Agent a read-only question first:

> "What's my Binance Agentic Wallet address and USDT balance?"

If the Agent replies that you are not signed in, the Skills are loaded correctly and you only need
to complete sign-in. If it does not recognize the request at all, the Skills were not picked up —
see below.

| Symptom                                 | Likely cause                          | Fix                                                               |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Agent doesn't recognize wallet requests | Skills installed in another directory | Re-run the install command in the folder your Agent is working in |
| `npx: command not found`                | Node.js missing or too old            | Install Node.js 18+ and re-check with `node -v`                   |
| Install succeeds but nothing changes    | Session started before install        | Restart the Agent session so it reloads its instructions          |
| Sign-in QR code expires before scanning | Link is short-lived                   | Ask the Agent to sign in again to get a fresh code                |

---

→ [Install Agentic Wallet](./install) — create your wallet and sign in

→ [Use Cases Overview](./use-cases/overview) — what to ask once you are connected

# Security & Settings

## 🎯 Goal

transaction handling — anytime through the Agent.

- Agentic Wallet [installed](../install) and signed in.

  current configuration, but not change it.

## Query your configuration

> "What's my current daily limit?"

> "What's my tradable token scope?"

> "Are high-risk transactions set to auto-reject or require confirmation?"

The Agent reads back your configuration in plain language — for example: "Your daily limit is
currently $5,000. Your tradable token scope is set to verified tokens only, and high-risk
transactions are set to require confirmation before they execute."

## Document: Minimal Tutorial

URL: /en/dev-docs/products/agentic-wallet/use-cases/minimal-tutorial


# Minimal Tutorial

## 🎯 Goal

Complete your first end-to-end swap in four steps — the shortest path from "is my wallet working" to
"the swap is on-chain".

## ✅ Prerequisites

- Agentic Wallet [installed](../install) and signed in.
- A small BNB balance for gas and the swap.

## Walkthrough

The minimal workflow: check status → get a quote → confirm and swap.

**1. Check wallet connection**

> "Is my wallet connected? What's my address?"

The Agent returns your connection status and wallet address.

**2. Check balances**

> "How much BNB and USDT do I have?"

The Agent returns all non-zero balances with USD valuation.

**3. Get a swap quote (no execution)**

> "How much USDT would I get for 0.01 BNB? Don't execute."

The Agent returns the estimated output, slippage, and gas estimate — no on-chain transaction is
triggered.

**4. Execute the swap**

> "Go ahead and execute."

The Agent requests your confirmation, then submits the on-chain swap and returns an order ID for
tracking.

## What's next

- Dive into [Wallet Operations](./basics/wallet-operations) for the full set of status and balance
  queries.
- Learn [Market Order](./trading/market-order) and [Limit Order](./trading/limit-order) trading in
  depth.



---

## Document: Developer Mode

URL: /en/dev-docs/products/agentic-wallet/use-cases/developer-mode


# Developer Mode

## 🎯 Goal

Go beyond the built-in operations: have your Agent preview and execute **contract calls you
construct yourself**, and produce **EIP-712 typed-data signatures** — with simulation, risk checks
and an explicit confirmation step in front of every action.

## ✅ Prerequisites

- Agentic Wallet [installed](../install) and signed in.
- **Developer Mode enabled in the Binance App.** It cannot be switched on by the Agent, by the CLI,
  or from the web — this is deliberate.

Check the current state before you try anything else:

> "Is Developer Mode enabled on my wallet?"

```bash
baw wallet settings --json
```

Look for `devMode.enabled`. If it is `false`, enable it in **Binance App → Agentic Wallet management
page → Settings**, then ask again. Four fields are worth reading before you script anything:

| Field                    | Meaning                                                                    |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `devMode.enabled`        | Whether external signing is currently allowed at all                       |
| `devMode.expiresAt`      | When Developer Mode lapses (Unix seconds); `null` when disabled or expired |
| `devMode.dailyLimit`     | The external-sign spend cap for a 24-hour period                           |
| `developerModeQuotaUsed` | How much of that cap has already been consumed today                       |

> **This quota is its own pool.** Developer Mode spending is independent of your main `dailyLimit`,
> and of the prediction, DeFi and x402 quotas — it neither consumes them nor is capped by them. Read
> `developerModeQuotaUsed` for Developer Mode usage, never `defiQuotaUsed` or `quotaUsed`.

---

## What Developer Mode does and does not change

By default, Agentic Wallet performs only capabilities that have been verified end to end — swap,
transfer, limit order, prediction market, tokenized securities, DeFi — and does not sign or initiate
arbitrary transactions. That is a security decision rather than a missing feature; see
[Verified Capabilities Only](../introduction#verified-capabilities-only) for the reasoning.

Developer Mode is the one exception, and it is deliberately narrow.

**What enabling it adds:**

- Arbitrary contract calls you construct — EVM `to` + calldata, or a Solana unsigned transaction.
- EIP-712 typed-data signatures for payloads you build yourself, such as Permit and Permit2.

**What does not move:**

| Boundary                  | Still applies                                                                                |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A separate spend cap**  | External signing draws on its own Developer Mode daily limit, set in the App                 |
| **Time-boxed access**     | Developer Mode expires — `devMode.expiresAt` — and must be re-enabled in the App             |
| **Risk interception**     | Operations assessed as high risk are blocked outright, before you can confirm them           |
| **Private key custody**   | Keys are MPC keyless and **cannot be exported** — there is no way to sign outside the wallet |
| **Two-step confirmation** | Every contract call and signature requires a preview and an explicit confirmation            |

The enable switch lives in the Binance App only — an Agent cannot turn Developer Mode on for itself,
which is why the prerequisite check above matters before you script anything against it.

---

## Supported signature types

Developer Mode widens what the Agent can do, but it does not lower the security floor. Message
signing stays restricted to structured data that can be parsed and shown to you before you approve
it:

| Signature type               | Method                       | Supported        |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------- |
| **EIP-712 typed data**       | `eth_signTypedData_v4`       | ✅ Yes           |
| **EIP-191 personal message** | `personal_sign` / `eth_sign` | ❌ Not supported |

`sign-message` accepts `--signType EIP712` only, and `--message` must be a full
`eth_signTypedData_v4` JSON-RPC request — not a plain string and not a pre-hashed digest.

**Why typed data only.** EIP-712 carries its own schema — domain, types, and the exact values being
authorised — so a preview can show you the spender, amounts and deadlines you are actually granting.
An EIP-191 plain-text message carries no structure at all: neither you nor the Agent can verify what
the resulting signature will be used for, which is exactly the property blind-signing attacks rely
on. Since an Agent signs without a human inspecting every payload, that class of request is not
permitted.

### What this means in practice

A large number of third-party flows ask you to sign a **plain text message** rather than structured
typed data. Common examples:

- "Sign in with Ethereum" style logins and dApp session authentication
- Airdrop, reward or points **claim** flows that verify address ownership by signing a sentence
- Allowlist or campaign registrations

All of these use EIP-191 `personal_sign`, and **they cannot be completed with an Agentic Wallet.**
This applies even when the activity that earned the reward was itself performed through Agentic
Wallet — for example, supplying liquidity or staking through the [DeFi](./trading/defi) flows, and
later being asked to sign a message to claim a distribution from that protocol.

Because keys cannot be exported, the signature cannot be produced elsewhere with the same address
either.

---

## The two-step safety flow

Every Developer Mode operation is deliberately split in two. The Agent will:

1. Run **preview** — parses the operation, simulates it, and returns risk information.
2. Show you the parsed transaction or message, any `risks`, and any authority being granted.
3. Wait for your **explicit confirmation**.
4. Run **execute**, using the `requestId` from that preview.

A preview that returns an error produces no `requestId` and cannot be executed. Previews also expire
— if execute reports an expired preview, simply preview again.

---

## Contract calls

> "Preview a contract call to 0xTargetContract on BSC with this calldata"

```bash
baw contract-call preview \
  --binanceChainId 56 \
  --from 0xYourAgentWallet \
  --to 0xTargetContract \
  --value 0 \
  --inputData 0x... \
  --json
```

| Parameter          | Required | Description                                                                   |
| ------------------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--binanceChainId` | Yes      | For example `56` (BSC), `1` (Ethereum), `CT_501` (Solana)                     |
| `--from`           | Yes      | Your Agentic Wallet address on that chain — ownership is verified server-side |
| `--to`             | EVM      | Target contract address                                                       |
| `--value`          | No       | Native value in **wei**, not human-readable. Integers only; decimals rejected |
| `--inputData`      | No       | EVM calldata, defaults to `0x`                                                |
| `--unsignedTx`     | Solana   | Base58-encoded unsigned transaction, used instead of `--to` / `--inputData`   |

> **Do not pass gas settings.** `contract-call` accepts no gas limit, gas price or gas option.
> Preview simulates directly, and execute uses backend gas estimation.

Then execute with the returned `requestId`:

```bash
baw contract-call execute --requestId a1b2c3d4... --json
```

**Reading the result:**

- `status: BROADCASTED` — signed and submitted; use the returned `txHash` to track it on-chain.
- `status: PENDING_CONFIRMATION` — you must approve in the Binance App before it completes.
- `requireConfirmation` in the preview tells you in advance which of the two to expect.
- `parsedTx.amount` is in the smallest unit. Divide by the token's `decimals` from `tokenInfos`
  before reading it as a human amount.

If the preview is intercepted, it returns an error and no `requestId` — the operation was assessed
as high risk and stopped before you could confirm it. There is nothing to execute in that case; the
error body carries the reason.

---

## Signing messages

> "Preview this EIP-712 signature request"

```bash
baw sign-message preview \
  --binanceChainId 1 \
  --signType EIP712 \
  --message '{"method":"eth_signTypedData_v4","params":["0xYourAgentWallet","{\"domain\":{...},\"primaryType\":\"Permit\",\"types\":{...},\"message\":{...}}"]}' \
  --json
```

`params[0]` must be your own Agentic Wallet address; `params[1]` is the EIP-712 typed data
(`domain`, `types`, `primaryType`, `message`) as a JSON string.

```bash
baw sign-message execute --requestId e5f6g7h8... --json
```

On success you get `status: COMPLETED` with `signature` and `signatureRecovery`. If it returns
`PENDING_CONFIRMATION`, approve in the App and then fetch the result:

```bash
baw sign-message result --order-id msg-order-xxx --json
```

`REJECTED` or `EXPIRED` means no signature will be produced.

> **Permit and Permit2:** these grant spending authority, not just a signature. Before confirming,
> read the `spender`, `sigDeadline` and each entry in `details[]` (token, amount, expiration) from
> `parsedMessage` — that is exactly what you are authorising.

---

## Signature history

> "Show me my recent message signatures"

```bash
baw sign-message history --binanceChainId 56 --limit 50 --json
```

Returns past signatures with `signatureTime`, `messageType`, and for Permit-style messages the
`spenderAddress`, `tokenPermits` and `signatureDeadline`. Use it to audit what authority your wallet
has granted over time. See also [Security & Settings](./security-settings) for reviewing and
revoking approvals.

---

- [Security & Settings](./security-settings) — daily limit, token scope, approvals
- [Automated Strategies](./automated-strategies) — combine Skills into end-to-end automation
- [Skills Reference](../skills-reference) — full capability reference

## Document: On-Chain Copy Trading

URL: /en/dev-docs/products/agentic-wallet/use-cases/copy-trading


# On-Chain Copy Trading

## 🎯 Goal

Follow smart-money addresses or on-chain signals continuously, and have every entry placed with
stop-loss and take-profit orders already on-chain — while you write the strategy and the scaffold
handles the plumbing.

> ⚠️ **This scaffold ships no strategy.** It gives you a running pipeline and three hooks where your
> own strategy goes. The hooks that come with it filter almost nothing and carry **no evidence of
> positive expectancy** — they exist to prove the pipeline runs, not to make money. Every risk
> control below is a _suggestion_, not a safeguard. On-chain transactions are irreversible and the
> risk is yours.

## ✅ Prerequisites

- Agentic Wallet [installed](../install) and signed in, on a chain that supports **both**
  `market-order` and `limit-order` (without limit orders you cannot place on-chain protection).
- A CLI at or above the floor the Skill declares in its frontmatter as `requiredCliVersion`
  (**1.9.1** at the time of writing) — that field is the single source of truth, so read it rather
  than this sentence. Below the floor the real-time connection has no keepalive and no reconnect,
  and the scaffold refuses to start:

  ```bash
  baw cli-check --required-version <the Skill's requiredCliVersion> --json
  ```

- These Skills, from
  [binance-skills-hub](https://github.com/binance/binance-skills-hub/tree/main/skills/binance-web3):
  `binance-onchain-copy-trader` plus `binance-agentic-wallet`, `binance-wallet-tracker`,
  `binance-leaderboard`, `binance-trading-signal`, `query-token-audit`.
- Python 3 on **Linux or macOS** — the single-instance lock uses `flock`, so Windows is not
  supported.
- A machine that stays awake, and **process-level supervision you set up yourself** (launchd,
  systemd, or a container restart policy). The scaffold restarts its own child processes, but
  nothing restarts the scaffold.

Check the environment before anything else:

```bash
baw --version
baw wallet status --json      # must be CONNECTED
baw wallet chains --json      # which chains are supported right now
baw wallet balance --binanceChainId <chain> --json   # quote token + native (gas)
```

Note that no cheap check proves a protective order will actually _place_. Treat a chain as
unverified until you have seen a real stop-loss reach `WORKING` on it, and do that first run at the
smallest size you are willing to hold unprotected.

## Step 1 · Install the Skill

> "Install the on-chain copy trader Skill and check whether its dependencies are all present"

The Agent installs `binance-onchain-copy-trader`, confirms the five dependency Skills are available,
and verifies the CLI version floor.

## Step 2 · Pick your trigger sources

Two peer real-time subscriptions. Use either, or both.

| Source      | What it follows                                    | How you choose                                                     |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Address** | Trades made by specific wallets you list           | Up to 100 addresses, one per line, in `$COPYTRADER_HOME/addrs.txt` |
| **Signal**  | The platform's own smart-money signals, all chains | No configuration needed                                            |

> "Find candidate addresses to copy on BSC, ranked by win rate, and score the top ones"

The Agent uses `binance-leaderboard` to list candidates and then scores each on six dimensions —
`follow_friendly` is the one that matters most here. Note that single dimensions saturate: over a
short window many addresses tie at 100% win rate, so add your own secondary criteria.

## Step 3 · Write the config

The first run writes an empty template to `$COPYTRADER_HOME` (default `~/.local/copytrader`) and
refuses to start until every required field is filled, listing exactly which are missing.

**There are no default values for anything that touches capital.** A stop-loss distance you never
thought about is as dangerous as a position size you never thought about. The single exception is
`mode`, which defaults to `dry-run` — an omission can never turn into live trading.

| Key                     | Meaning                                                                      |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `chain` / `quote_token` | Chain ID and quote-token address (lowercase)                                 |
| `sources`               | `["address"]`, `["signal"]`, or both                                         |
| `budget_usd`            | Cumulative deployment cap. **Decide whether losing all of it is acceptable** |
| `position_usd`          | Per-trade size                                                               |
| `max_positions`         | Concurrent position cap                                                      |
| `gas_floor_native`      | Native-token floor; also stops if the balance cannot be read                 |
| `policy.*`              | Your strategy parameters — passed to your hooks verbatim                     |

Leave `mode` as `dry-run`.

## Step 4 · Dry-run with the bundled hooks unchanged

```bash
cd <skill-dir>/scripts && python3 copytrader.py
tail -f $COPYTRADER_HOME/copytrader.log
```

**Do not edit the hooks yet.** What ships filters almost nothing, which makes it a poor strategy but
a good instrument: it lets through a broad sample so you can see what the stream actually contains
before you start rejecting things.

At this point you are answering one question only — _does the plumbing work?_ Check that the startup
log matches what you intended, that events are arriving from every source you configured, and that
the `decision` distribution in `events.jsonl` shows each gate rejecting what you expect.

**Do not read a dry-run pass rate as a live fill rate.** Dry-run records no positions, so the budget
and concurrency guardrails never fire — it will always pass more than live would open.

## Step 5 · Score the decisions before spending anything

Every decision that _would have opened a position_ — dry-run included, where nothing is bought —
re-reads the price at `outcome_horizons_min` (default `[5, 15, 60]`) and appends it to
`outcomes.jsonl`. Join it with `events.jsonl` on the event key and you get one row per decision
carrying both its features and its forward return:

> "Read my outcomes.jsonl and tell me which event features actually separated winners from losers"

These numbers are **marks, not fills** — no slippage, fees, token tax or gas, and a horizon is an
instant rather than a path, so a good reading at 60 minutes says nothing about whether a stop-loss
would have been touched first. Treat them as an upper bound, and let sample size govern how much you
conclude.

## Step 6 · Write your strategy

Three functions at the top of `scripts/copytrader.py`. The mechanism layer never touches them:

```python
should_enter(ev, ctx)  -> (bool, reason)
size_position(ev, ctx) -> float          # USD
exit_plan(ev, ctx, entry_price, qty) -> [(trigger_price, sell_qty, slippage_pct), ...]
```

`should_enter` is called **twice** — once before anything has been spent on audit and market data,
and once after both are ready. Put cheap judgements in the first call and anything needing audit
data in the second.

Build your thresholds from **your own** dataset from step 5. Numbers copied from someone else's run
describe their sample, their sources and their window — not yours.

## Step 7 · Go live

Switch `mode` to `live`. The run refuses to start unless `$COPYTRADER_HOME/I_UNDERSTAND_THE_RISK`
contains the current `budget_usd`:

```bash
echo <budget_usd> > $COPYTRADER_HOME/I_UNDERSTAND_THE_RISK
```

Requiring the _amount_ rather than mere existence means the acknowledgement cannot be inherited by
copying someone else's runtime directory, and that **raising `budget_usd` invalidates it** — more
money at risk deserves a fresh decision. An Agent may write this file once you have confirmed the
number; what matters is that the decision was made about this specific amount.

Start with an amount whose total loss is acceptable.

## Operating a live run

| Action                     | Command                                     |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Stop opening new positions | `touch $COPYTRADER_HOME/STOP`               |
| Exit the process           | `touch $COPYTRADER_HOME/KILL`               |
| Restore the live gate      | `rm $COPYTRADER_HOME/I_UNDERSTAND_THE_RISK` |

> "Summarize my copy-trading run: open positions, realized P&L, and what the gates rejected most"

**Process exit does not cancel protective orders already on-chain.** Stopping the runner leaves your
stop-loss and take-profit orders working; cancelling them is a separate, explicit action.

## Known limitations

| Limitation                             | What it means for you                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Structural lag**                     | Your fill is necessarily later than the address you copy. If they are the issuer or hold a private execution path, their gains are not reproducible while their losses copy in full |
| **Market orders fill at market**       | A stop-loss trigger price is a trigger, not a fill price. In a fast drop the fill can be well below it                                                                              |
| **There is an unprotected window**     | Time passes between the buy filling and the protective order being placed. The position has no downside protection in that window — it can be shortened, not eliminated             |
| **No protection without limit orders** | On a chain where `limit-order` is unavailable, protection depends entirely on the process staying alive                                                                             |
| **The scaffold has no supervisor**     | It restarts its own child processes, but if the scaffold itself exits nothing brings it back. That is your job to configure                                                         |
| **Version coupling is hard**           | Below CLI 1.9.1 a dropped connection goes permanently silent, and silence is indistinguishable from a quiet market                                                                  |

## What's next

- [Automated Strategies](./automated-strategies) — conversational strategies that need no
  long-running process.
- [Skills Reference](../skills-reference) — full capability reference for all Skills modules.
- [Security Settings](./security-settings) — wallet-level limits that apply regardless of strategy.

> ⚠️ **Risk warning:** Nothing here is investment advice. The scaffold guarantees only that it will
> run the checks you configure — not that those checks are sufficient to protect your funds.



---

## Document: Automated Trading Strategies

URL: /en/dev-docs/products/agentic-wallet/use-cases/automated-strategies


# Automated Trading Strategies

## 🎯 Goal

Combine Agentic Wallet with published Wallet Skills to build end-to-end automated trading strategies
— discover opportunities, run security checks, and execute trades from a single conversation.

## ✅ Prerequisites

- Agentic Wallet [installed](../install) and signed in.
- **The strategies below require the corresponding Skills to be installed.** Get them from
  [binance-skills-hub](https://github.com/binance/binance-skills-hub/tree/main/skills/binance-web3):
  - Strategy 1 (Meme Sniping): `meme-rush`, `query-token-audit`
  - Strategy 2 (Smart Money): `trading-signal`, `query-token-audit`
  - Strategy 3 (Narrative Capture): `meme-rush`, `query-token-info`

## Strategy 1: Meme Token Sniping

Use `meme-rush` to monitor newly launched or migrating Meme tokens, run security pre-checks with
`query-token-audit`, and execute trades when safe.

**Example conversation:**

> "What new Meme tokens launched on Solana recently?"

The Agent uses `meme-rush` to return tokens on the bonding curve.

> "Audit the security of token XXX for me"

The Agent uses `query-token-audit` to return risk score, honeypot detection, tax analysis, etc.

> "Looks safe enough. Buy with 50 USDT"

The Agent confirms and executes a market swap via Agentic Wallet.

## Strategy 2: Smart Money Following

Use `trading-signal` to monitor smart money buy signals in real-time, auto-check security, and
follow trades.

**Basic usage:**

> "What are the latest smart money buy signals?"

The Agent uses `trading-signal` to return active signals with token, trigger price, current price,
max gain, etc.

> "Is the token from this signal safe? Check it for me"

The Agent calls `query-token-audit` to return the security audit.

> "Looks good, buy with 50 USDT"

The Agent executes the trade via Agentic Wallet.

**Advanced usage — automated following:**

> "Check smart money signals every 5 minutes. When a new signal appears, auto-audit it. If risk
> level is LOW, buy with 50 USDT"

The AI Agent will set up a scheduled task to automatically: fetch signals → security audit → execute
trade if safe. The specific implementation is planned by the Agent based on your instructions.

## Strategy 3: Narrative Trend Capture

Use `meme-rush`'s AI narrative detection to discover market hot spots and position early.

**Example conversation:**

> "What narratives are trending right now? Which themes have the most capital inflow?"

The Agent uses `meme-rush` to return narrative themes ranked by net capital inflow.

> "What are the representative tokens for this narrative?"

The Agent returns related tokens with market data.

> "Check the holder distribution and liquidity for XXX"

The Agent uses `query-token-info` to return token details, holder analytics, and liquidity data.

> "Liquidity looks deep. Set a limit sell order for 50% when it reaches $1.2"

The Agent creates a limit sell order via Agentic Wallet.

## Best Practices

| Principle               | Description                                                                 |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Audit before buying** | For any non-mainstream token, audit with `query-token-audit` before trading |
| **Start small**         | Test new strategies with small amounts before scaling up                    |
| **Set stop-losses**     | Use limit sell orders to define exit points and avoid being stuck           |
| **Diversify**           | Don't put all funds into a single token or narrative                        |
| **Monitor regularly**   | Check limit order status and portfolio changes periodically                 |

> ⚠️ **Risk Warning:** On-chain trading involves slippage, MEV attacks, and contract risks. All
> trading decisions should be based on your own research (DYOR). Skills provide information and
> execution capabilities only — they do not constitute investment advice.

## What's next

- [Skills Reference](../skills-reference) — Full capability reference for all Skills modules.
- [Supported Skills](../../wallet-skills/introduction) — View all available Wallet Skills.

## Document: Tokenized Securities

URL: /en/dev-docs/products/agentic-wallet/use-cases/trading/tokenized-securities


# Tokenized Securities

## 🎯 Goal

Research and trade tokenized stocks (bStock and Ondo) by ticker or company name in plain language —
look up the on-chain price and trading status, then buy or sell the stock token, all through
conversation with your AI Agent.

## ✅ Prerequisites

- Agentic Wallet [installed](../../install) and signed in.
- **Install the
  [`binance-tokenized-securities-info`](https://github.com/binance/binance-skills-hub/tree/main/skills/binance-web3)
  skill.** Agentic Wallet uses it to resolve a ticker/company name to its on-chain contract and to
  fetch price, fundamentals, and trading status. Without it, the Agent can't map "AAPL" to a
  tradable token.
- USDT to buy, plus native token (BNB) for gas.

## How it works

A tokenized stock is an on-chain token backed by the underlying share. Trading it uses the same swap
flow as any token — the extra step is **resolving the ticker to a contract and checking the token's
trading status first**:

1. **Resolve** — the Agent maps the ticker or company name to its on-chain contract.
2. **Check status** — confirm the token is tradable (not paused / halted for a corporate action).
3. **Trade** — buy or sell the stock token.

## Research a stock

> "What tokenized stocks are available?"

The Agent lists the tradable bStock and Ondo tickers.

> "What's the on-chain price of AAPL, and its P/E and 52-week range?"

The Agent replies in plain language — for example: "AAPL is trading at about $228.5 on-chain. Its
P/E is 31.4, the dividend yield is 0.44%, and the 52-week range is $169.21–$260.10."

> "Show me TSLA's holders, circulating supply, and market cap"

The Agent summarizes the on-chain data for you conversationally.

## Check trading status before you trade

Tokenized stocks follow session states and corporate actions — a token can be paused or halted.

> "Is AAPL tradable right now?"

The Agent tells you the current state — for example: "AAPL is open and trading normally (regular
session), next close is 8:00 PM UTC." If a token is halted for a corporate action (earnings,
dividend, split, merger, or maintenance), the Agent explains why and holds off on trading.

## Buy a tokenized stock

> "How much AAPL would I get for 100 USDT? Quote only."

The Agent replies with the estimate — for example: "100 USDT would get you about 0.437 AAPL at the
current price, with 0.5% slippage. No order placed."

> "Buy AAPL with 100 USDT"

The Agent resolves the contract, checks status, shows you the quote, and on your confirmation
submits the swap — then confirms: "Done — your buy order for AAPL is submitted. Ask me to check its
status anytime."

## Sell a tokenized stock

> "Sell half my TSLA position for USDT"

> "Sell all my NVDA tokens"

The Agent confirms the amount and destination before executing, then reports back once the sell is
submitted.

## Check order status

> "Did my AAPL buy go through?"

The Agent looks up the order and answers in plain language — for example: "Yes — your AAPL buy
filled successfully. You spent 100 USDT and the transaction is confirmed on-chain."

## Automated strategies

Beyond one-off trades, you can hand the Agent a rule and let it watch a stock and act for you over
the long run.

### Example 1 — Earnings-reaction watcher

> "Watch NVDA on an ongoing basis. Around each earnings report, track how the price reacts: if it
> drops more than 8% from the pre-earnings level, buy 100 USDT as a dip; if I'm holding and it's up
> more than 10%, take profit on half. Keep this running across future earnings and message me on
> each action."

The Agent runs continuously, watches each earnings reaction as it comes, applies your dip-buy and
take-profit rules, executes when one triggers, and reports every move — staying active until you
stop it.

### Example 2 — News-driven sector strategy

Have the Agent continuously monitor market news, judge the impact on a sector you hold, and manage
the position or rotate into a new name.

> "Keep an eye on AI and semiconductor news — new model releases, chip export rules, key
> supply-chain moves. If clearly bullish news for AI/semis breaks and I hold NVDA or AMD, add 50
> USDT to the stronger one; if it names a tradable stock I don't hold yet (say a new AI winner), buy
> 50 USDT as a starter; if clearly bearish news breaks, trim my AI/semi exposure by 30%. Run this
> for 7 days and tell me each time, with the reason."

Over those 7 days the Agent keeps monitoring, judges each news item as bullish or bearish for
AI/semis and maps it to your holdings, decides whether to scale up, open a new position, or trim,
checks the token's on-chain trading status before acting, then executes and explains its reasoning.

> 💡 **Tip:** Agentic Wallet focuses on on-chain trading. Off-chain data such as earnings or news
> must be supplied via your own data source or a relevant Skill.

## ⚠️ Risk notice

Tokenized securities are not covered by securities insurance, may be restricted in your
jurisdiction, and can be halted for corporate actions. On-chain trading also carries slippage and
smart-contract risk. Do your own research (DYOR) — Skills provide information and execution
capability only, never investment advice.



---

## Document: Prediction Market

URL: /en/dev-docs/products/agentic-wallet/use-cases/trading/prediction-market


# Prediction Market

## 🎯 Goal

Trade prediction markets end-to-end in natural language — discover markets, place market or limit
bets on outcomes, track positions and PnL, redeem winnings after a market resolves, and even hand
the whole loop to an automated strategy.

## ✅ Prerequisites

- Agentic Wallet [installed](../../install) and signed in.
- BSC USDT balance to fund bets (prediction trades are quoted and settled in USDT).

## Browse & discover markets

Explore what's tradable by category, popularity, or keyword.

> "What prediction market categories are available?"

The Agent lists the categories — for example: crypto, sports, politics, economy, and culture.

> "Show me the most popular markets in the crypto category"

> "List crypto markets sorted by volume"

> "Search prediction markets about the next Fed rate decision"

The Agent returns the matching markets with their current odds and volume, and can sort by
recommended, volume, participants, newest, or soonest-to-resolve.

## Inspect a market before betting

> "Show me the full detail of this market"

> "What are the current odds for the 'Yes' outcome?"

> "What was the last traded price on this market?"

The Agent summarizes the market — the question, resolution date, each outcome's implied probability,
and recent activity. Prices sit between 0 and 1 USDT and read as the market's implied probability,
so a "Yes" at 0.62 means the market prices that outcome at ~62%.

> **Note:** the last-traded price is a historical fill, not a live quote — it can be stale. The
> Agent always pulls a fresh quote before placing an order.

## Place a bet

Prediction trading always quotes first, then places on your confirmation.

> "Buy 'Up' in the most recent BTC 15m price market with 5 USDT"

The Agent replies with the quote in plain language — for example: "5 USDT buys about 8.1 shares of
'Up' at an average price of 0.61, with a 1.2% price impact and a 0.02 USDT fee. Confirm to place?"
On your confirmation it places the order and reports back.

Both **market** and **limit** orders are supported:

> "Place a limit buy for 'Yes' at 0.60 USDT with 20 USDT"

> "Sell 10 shares of my 'Up' position at market"

A **buy** amount is the USDT you spend; a **sell** amount is the number of shares you sell.

## Check positions & PnL

> "What are my current prediction positions?"

> "Show my prediction portfolio and unrealized PnL"

> "Show my settled positions — only the ones I won"

The Agent groups your positions into ongoing, ended, and ready-to-claim, and summarizes your PnL —
for example: "You hold 3 ongoing positions worth ~42 USDT, up 11% unrealized. One resolved position
is ready to claim."

## Track & cancel orders

> "Show my prediction order history"

> "Which of my prediction orders are still open?"

> "Cancel my pending prediction order"

The Agent lists your orders with their status and can cancel any that are still resting. Placing an
order isn't the same as it filling — market orders usually fill quickly, while limit orders rest
until the price is hit, so the Agent always verifies status before reporting a bet as complete.

## Redeem winnings

Once a market resolves in your favor, claim the payout:

> "Do I have any winning predictions ready to claim?"

> "Redeem my winning prediction positions"

The Agent finds your ready-to-claim positions and triggers the redemption on-chain, then confirms
the payout landed in your wallet.

## Automated strategies

Beyond manual bets, you can hand the whole loop to the Agent and let it watch, judge, and bet on the
BTC 5-minute "Up / Down" market for you over the long run.

### Example — Price-trend-based Up/Down betting

> "Keep tracking BTC's price action and pull the settlement results of the last few 5-minute Up/Down
> rounds. Before each round settles, run a technical read on that price data — say short-term
> moving-average direction and recent momentum — to judge whether the next 5 minutes is more likely
> to settle Up or Down, then bet 10 USDT on the side you favor. Keep my total open exposure in the
> BTC 5-minute Up/Down market under 50 USDT, take profit once the overall position is up +30% and
> cut losses at −20%, and tell me the direction and reasoning on every bet."

The Agent keeps tracking price action and each round's outcome, runs a technical read before every
round to form a directional view, bets on that side within your 50 USDT exposure cap, and watches
overall PnL to apply the +30% take-profit and −20% stop-loss — reporting the direction and reason on
each action, until you stop it.

> 💡 **Tip:** Agentic Wallet focuses on prediction-market trading. BTC price data must be supplied
> via your own data source or a relevant Skill.

## ⚠️ Risk notice

Prediction outcomes are binary — a position can go to zero if the market resolves against you, and
outcome-token liquidity can be thin. Resolution depends on the market's oracle. Do your own research
(DYOR) — Skills provide information and execution capability only, never investment advice.

## What's next

- [Tokenized Securities](./tokenized-securities) — Trade tokenized stocks (bStock and Ondo).
- [DeFi](./defi) — Earn yield, provide liquidity, and manage protocol positions.
- [Automated Strategies](../automated-strategies) — Automate discovery and trading with Skills.

## Document: Market Order (Swap)

URL: /en/dev-docs/products/agentic-wallet/use-cases/trading/market-order


# Market Order (Swap)

## 🎯 Goal

Swap one token for another at the current market price — get a quote first, then confirm to execute,
and track the order to completion.

## ✅ Prerequisites

- Agentic Wallet [installed](../../install) and signed in.
- Enough balance of the token you're selling, plus native token for gas.

## Get a quote

> "How much USDT would I get for 0.1 BNB? Quote only, don't execute."

The Agent replies with the estimate in plain language — for example: "0.1 BNB is currently worth
about 61 USDT, with 0.5% slippage and a small gas fee. No transaction placed."

## Execute a market swap

> "Swap 0.1 BNB for USDT"

> "Buy BNB with 50 USDT, slippage max 2%"

The Agent shows the quote and waits for confirmation. Say "confirm" or "go ahead" to trigger the
swap.

## Check order status

> "Has my last swap completed?"

> "Show me my recent swap orders"

> "Any swaps still pending?"

The Agent summarizes your orders in plain language — for example: "Your last swap of 0.1 BNB for
about 61 USDT finished successfully a few minutes ago. You have no swaps still pending." The status
of each order maps to one of the following:

| Status     | Description           |
| ---------- | --------------------- |
| `PENDING`  | Processing on-chain   |
| `FINISHED` | Executed successfully |
| `FAILED`   | Execution failed      |

## ⚠️ Risk notice

Market swaps execute at the best available price, which means slippage can be significant on
illiquid or volatile pairs — the amount you receive may differ from the quote. On-chain trading also
carries MEV-attack and smart-contract risk. Always review the final quote the Agent shows before
confirming, and base every decision on your own research (DYOR) — Skills provide information and
execution capability only, never investment advice.

## What's next

- [Limit Order](./limit-order) — Set a target price and let the Agent execute automatically.
- [Automated Strategies](../automated-strategies) — Combine swaps with Skills for hands-off trading.



---

## Document: Limit Order

URL: /en/dev-docs/products/agentic-wallet/use-cases/trading/limit-order


# Limit Order

## 🎯 Goal

Set a target price once and let the Agent execute the trade automatically when the market hits it —
no need to watch the charts.

## ✅ Prerequisites

- Agentic Wallet [installed](../../install) and signed in.
- **Chain support:** limit orders are only available on **BSC and Solana**.
- **Token rules:** buy orders — `fromToken` must be USDT, USDC, USD1, U or native token; sell orders
  — `toToken` must be USDT, USDC, USD1, U or native token.

## Place a limit buy

> "Buy BNB with 100 USDT when the price drops to $500"

> "When WETH drops to $2800, buy some with 200 USDT on BSC"

The Agent creates the conditional order and returns a strategy ID. It executes automatically when
the price is hit.

## Place a limit sell

> "Sell 1 BNB for USDT when the price reaches $650"

> "Sell 0.5 WETH on BSC when it hits $3500"

The Agent sets up the sell order and confirms in plain language — for example: "I've placed a limit
sell for 1 BNB at $650 (strategy ID 9876543210). It will execute automatically once the price is
reached."

## Check limit orders

> "What limit orders do I have open?"

> "Show me limit orders still waiting to trigger"

> "Check the status of limit order 9876543210"

The Agent summarizes your open orders in plain language — for example: "You have one open order: a
limit sell of 1 BNB at $650, still waiting for the trigger price." Each order's status maps to one
of the following:

| Status      | Description               |
| ----------- | ------------------------- |
| `WORKING`   | Waiting for trigger price |
| `TRIGGERED` | Price hit, executing      |
| `PENDING`   | Processing on-chain       |
| `FINISHED`  | Executed successfully     |
| `FAILED`    | Execution failed          |
| `EXPIRED`   | Order expired             |
| `CANCELED`  | Order canceled            |

## Cancel a limit order

> "Cancel my BNB limit buy order"

> "Cancel all my open orders"

The Agent confirms the cancellation in plain language — for example: "Done — your BNB limit buy
order has been canceled and is no longer resting on the book."

## ⚠️ Risk notice

Limit orders rest on the book until the trigger price is hit — they are **not** guaranteed to fill,
and a resting sell does not protect against a price gap that blows through your trigger. On-chain
trading also involves slippage, MEV attacks, and smart-contract risk. Every decision should be based
on your own research (DYOR) — Skills provide information and execution capability only, never
investment advice.

## What's next

- [Market Order](./market-order) — Swap immediately at market price instead.
- [Automated Strategies](../automated-strategies) — Use limit sells as automated stop-losses.

## Document: DeFi

URL: /en/dev-docs/products/agentic-wallet/use-cases/trading/defi


# DeFi

## 🎯 Goal

Put your assets to work across DeFi protocols — browse products, deposit to earn, redeem, provide or
remove liquidity, claim rewards, monitor positions and set alerts (including lending health factor),
and even hand ongoing monitoring and rebalancing to an automated strategy — all through
conversation.

## ✅ Prerequisites

- Agentic Wallet [installed](../../install) and signed in.
- Enough balance of the asset you want to deposit or provide, plus native token for gas.

## Browse protocols & investment products

> "What DeFi protocols are supported?"

> "Show me earn options for USDT"

> "What's the APY for depositing BNB?"

> "List available LP pools"

The Agent walks you through the options in plain language — for example: "Supported protocols
include Venus (lending & earn), Lista DAO (BNB staking), and PancakeSwap (liquidity). For USDT earn,
Venus is offering around 4.2% APY, and depositing BNB into Lista DAO earns roughly 3.8%. There are
also LP pools such as BNB/USDT and ETH/USDT on PancakeSwap."

> **Note:** APY and rewards shown are live examples that change constantly — the Agent always pulls
> fresh rates before you act, and the numbers above are illustrative only.

## Check DeFi positions

> "What are my current DeFi positions?"

> "How much am I earning?"

> "Show me my LP positions — are any out of range?"

> "Do I have any claimable rewards?"

The Agent summarizes your positions in plain language — for example: "You have 100 USDT supplied on
Venus earning ~4.2% APY, and a BNB/USDT LP position on PancakeSwap that's currently in range. You
have about 0.8 USDT of unclaimed rewards ready to collect."

## Deposit

> "Deposit 100 USDT to Venus"

> "Deposit 0.5 BNB into Lista DAO"

The Agent shows a transaction preview before execution — for example: "Depositing 100 USDT to Venus:
you'll receive ~100 vUSDT, estimated APY ~4.2%, gas ~0.15 USD, contract 0x…. Confirm to proceed?" On
your confirmation it executes and reports back.

## Redeem

> "Redeem my USDT from Venus"

> "Redeem all my BNB from Lista DAO"

The Agent previews the redemption and confirms once it's done — for example: "I've redeemed your 100
USDT from Venus plus about 0.4 USDT of accrued interest. The funds are back in your wallet."

## Check & monitor lending health factor

For lending positions, ask about your health factor and borrow exposure at any time, or have the
Agent watch it and alert you.

> "What's my lending health factor on Venus?"

> "What am I borrowing on Venus?"

> "Alert me when my health factor on Venus drops below 1.5."

The Agent reads your position and reports in plain language — for example: "Your Venus lending
health factor is 1.85. You're borrowing 50 USDT against 100 USDT of supplied collateral. Health
factor above 1.0 is safe; the closer it gets to 1.0, the higher the liquidation risk."

> **Note:** lending health factor and borrow data are **read-only** here — the Agent can query and
> monitor them and alert you, but borrowing and repayment are not executed through the Agentic
> Wallet. Manage those actions in the lending protocol directly.

## Add liquidity

> "Add liquidity to the BNB/USDT pool on PancakeSwap"

> "Provide 500 USDT and equivalent BNB to PancakeSwap BNB/USDT"

For concentrated liquidity pools, the Agent uses the protocol's default price range unless you
specify otherwise. It previews the pairing and confirms once the position is open — for example:
"I've added 500 USDT and about 0.8 BNB to the PancakeSwap BNB/USDT pool. Your LP position is now
active and in range."

## Remove liquidity

> "Remove my liquidity from PancakeSwap BNB/USDT pool"

> "Remove 50% of my LP position on PancakeSwap"

The Agent confirms the withdrawal in plain language — for example: "I've removed 50% of your
BNB/USDT LP position. About 250 USDT and 0.4 BNB have been returned to your wallet, along with any
fees earned."

## Claim rewards / LP fee / redemption

> "Claim my LP fee income from PancakeSwap"

> "Claim my redemption assets of Lista DAO"

The Agent claims and confirms in plain language — for example: "I've claimed your accrued LP fees
from PancakeSwap — about 0.8 USDT and a small amount of BNB have been credited to your wallet."

## Transaction status

After submitting a DeFi transaction, you can check its status:

> "Has my deposit to Venus gone through?"

> "Check my recent DeFi transactions"

The Agent reports the status in plain language — for example: "Your 100 USDT deposit to Venus was
confirmed on-chain a moment ago and now shows in your positions. Your other recent DeFi transactions
have all completed successfully." Each transaction's status maps to one of the following:

| Status    | Description                                           |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `PENDING` | Transaction broadcast, awaiting on-chain confirmation |
| `SUCCESS` | Executed successfully                                 |
| `FAILED`  | Transaction reverted on-chain                         |

## Post-trade verification

After every DeFi transaction, the Agent automatically verifies:

1. On-chain transaction receipt (success/revert)
2. Position balance change matches expected amount
3. Updated position reflected in portfolio
4. App push notification sent with result

## Automated strategies

Beyond one-off actions, you can hand the Agent a standing rule and let it watch a position and act
for you over the long run — no need to check in manually.

### Example — Monitor and auto-rebalance an out-of-range LP

Give the Agent a rule to keep watching an LP position, alert you, and rebalance it automatically
when it drifts out of range.

> "Monitor my BNB/USDT LP on PancakeSwap continuously. Alert me if it goes out of range, and
> rebalance it automatically: remove the position, re-center a new range around the current price,
> and re-add the same liquidity. Keep doing this and message me on every alert and rebalance with
> the new range and any fees collected."

The Agent watches your LP's range status round the clock — for example: "Monitoring your BNB/USDT LP
on PancakeSwap. It's in range now (price 0.61, range 0.55–0.68). I'll alert you the moment it drifts
out." The moment price drifts outside your active range, it alerts you, removes the position, opens
a fresh one centered on the current price with the same liquidity, re-enters, and reports the new
range plus any fees claimed — repeating on each drift until you stop it.

> 💡 **Tip:** Automated monitoring runs continuously and acts on-chain within your rules. Set clear
> thresholds and caps, and keep enough wallet balance for the follow-up action (e.g. tokens for the
> LP pairing, gas). Any off-chain data must be supplied via your own data source or a relevant
> Skill.

## ⚠️ Risk notice

DeFi deposits and liquidity provision are not risk-free: protocols carry smart-contract risk
(undetected bugs, hacks), you may be exposed to impermanent loss, and APY/rewards are variable and
not guaranteed. If you hold a lending position, its health factor can fall and lead to liquidation —
the Agent can monitor and alert you, but does not borrow or repay on your behalf. Automated rules
act on-chain on your behalf — a rebalance can still fail or fill at an unfavorable price under
fast-moving markets. On-chain trading also involves slippage, MEV attacks, and gas-price volatility.
Always confirm the contract address the Agent previews before approving, and base every decision on
your own research (DYOR) — Skills provide information and execution capability only, never
investment advice.

## What's next

- [Market Order](./market-order) — Swap tokens to fund your DeFi positions.
- [Automated Strategies](../automated-strategies) — Combine DeFi with Skills for hands-off yield.

## Document: bStock AI PnL Trading Competition

# bStock AI PnL Trading Competition

## 🚀 Already Registered? Check how to trade with your Agent

> **Not registered yet** → complete [Registration](#-registration) first. **Already registered** →
> follow the four steps below to start competing.

The Agentic Wallet is a wallet for an **AI Agent** (Claude / Codex / Openclaw, etc.) — every
campaign action is done by **talking to your Agent**, with no manual commands. If you've never used
an Agent, here's the whole flow (copy each prompt to your Agent):

**1. Have your Agent install the BAW Skill.** Copy the following prompt to your Agent and ask it to
install — this is what lets the Agent operate the wallet, trade bStock, and complete the AI tasks:

```text
Install the Binance Agentic Wallet skill from
https://github.com/binance/binance-skills-hub/tree/main/skills/binance-web3/binance-agentic-wallet
```

> 💡 You can install and sign in in one go — e.g. "Install the Binance Agentic Wallet Skill and
> start the sign-in process". The Agent installs the Skill and reports the connection status:

<img
  src="/en/dev-docs/aw_campaign_signin_demo_en.png"
  alt="Example: the Agent installs the BAW Skill, signs in, and reports Connected with session details"
  width="380"
/>

**2. Sign in to the Agentic Wallet.** Copy the following prompt to your Agent. The Agent returns a
QR code / link to scan with the Binance App — confirm the pairing code and accept the security
checks. **After signing in, deposit funds to your wallet address before trading.** For the full
sign-in walkthrough, see [Install/Sign-in Documentation](../../install) for the detailed guide.

```text
Sign in to Agentic Wallet
```

<img
  src="/en/dev-docs/aw_signin_flow.png"
  alt="Agentic Wallet sign-in flow: confirm the pairing code, then accept the three security checks"
  width="720"
/>

**3. Complete the two AI tasks.** CMC (market data) and BNB Chain Agent Studio (single-stock report)
are **mandatory for eligibility** (see
[Complete the AI-Analysis Tasks](#complete-the-ai-analysis-tasks) below), use the following prompt
to let your Agent do it for you:

```text
Check the campaign and finish the CMC & BNB Chain Agent Studio tasks
```

**4. Trade bStock.** Trade per your strategy to climb the leaderboard and share the prize pool. See
the [eligible list](./bstock-eligible-tokens) (tokens with the 🏆 icon are eligible), you can also
use the following prompt to let your Agent check what is eligible and trade it for you:

```text
Buy an eligible bStock token
```

> 💡 You can also combine it all in one prompt — e.g. finish the AI tasks and place a trade
> together:

<img
  src="/en/dev-docs/aw_campaign_agent_demo_en.png"
  alt="Example: one prompt asks the Agent to finish the CMC & Agent Studio tasks and buy 100 USDT of NVDA"
  width="380"
/>

## 🎯 Overview

The bStock AI PnL Trading Competition is jointly run by Binance Wallet, bStocks, BNB Chain Agent
Studio, and CoinMarketCap. Participants trade tokenized US stocks (bStock) through the Agentic
Wallet, using two types of AI analysis (crypto market sentiment and single-stock research) to inform
decisions.

Ranking is based not on trading volume but on **Realized PnL (realized profit and loss — the portion
actually sold)** — the defining difference from an ordinary trading contest.

## 📅 At a Glance

| Item                | Detail                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Period**          | 2026-08-17 09:00:00 ~ 2026-09-01 00:00:00 (UTC)                          |
| **Ranking**         | Realized PnL absolute value, high to low — Top 100 share the prize pool  |
| **Prize pool**      | Up to 100,000 USDC, unlocked in tiers by total participant bStock AUM    |
| **Chain**           | BNB Smart Chain (BSC)                                                    |
| **Eligible tokens** | Weekly [eligible bStock list](./bstock-eligible-tokens) (updated weekly) |
| **Reward payout**   | USDC, sent to the participating Agentic Wallet                           |

> The figures above are indicative — **campaign dates, prize tiers, and required call counts are all
> per the official campaign page**.

## 📝 Registration

> ⚠️ **Registration is done on the Binance App / Web, not within the Agent.** Registration cannot be
> done by the AI Agent — this step must be performed in person on the campaign page. Only trades
> after registration count toward the campaign, and **the bound wallet cannot be changed once
> confirmed** — be sure to bind the Agentic Wallet you will use to participate.

Registration can be completed on the **App** or on the **Web**. Enter the bStock campaign page
first:

- **Web**:
  [web3.binance.com/en/activity/unified-tc/agentic-pnl](https://web3.binance.com/en/activity/unified-tc/agentic-pnl)
- **App**: copy the deep link below and open it in the Binance App (desktop browsers cannot launch
  it):

```text
bnc://app.binance.com/mp/app?appId=xoqXxUSMRccLCrZNRebmzj&startPagePath=cGFnZXMvc3VicGFja2FnZXMvdW5pZmllZC10Yy9pbmRleA%3D%3D&startPageQuery=YWN0aXZpdHlJZD1hZ2VudGljLXBubA%3D%3D&showOptions=2
```

> 💡 **If you don't have an Agentic Wallet yet, register on the App.** The Web cannot create an
> Agentic Wallet directly — it can only register an existing one — whereas the App can create one
> during registration.

### 📱 Register on the App

1. **Tap [Join] to register.** Tap the **Join** button at the bottom of the campaign page.
2. **(If you don't have an Agentic Wallet yet) tap [Create Now].** If your account has no Agentic
   Wallet, a **"Create Your Agentic Wallet First"** prompt appears — tap **Create Now** to start
   creation. **Skip steps 2–4 if you already have one.**
3. **Create the wallet.** Tick **"I agree to enable Secure Auto Sign"**, accept the terms, and tap
   **Create Agentic Wallet** — the App creates it automatically.
4. **Tap [Back] once created.** When **"Wallet ready!"** appears, tap **Back** to return to the
   campaign page.
5. **Tap [Join] again and confirm the participating wallet.** In the **Confirm Participate** dialog,
   verify the Agentic Wallet address under **Select Wallet**, then tap **Confirm**. **Each user may
   register only once, and the wallet cannot be changed once confirmed.**
6. **Registration succeeds.** When **"Your Agent Is Ready to Trade"** appears, registration is
   complete; eligible trades via that wallet begin counting toward the campaign.

  src="/en/dev-docs/aw_campaign_app_flow.png"
  alt="App registration flow: Join → Create Now → Create Wallet → Wallet ready → Confirm Participate → Success"
  width="1120"
/>

The Web flow is for users who **already have an Agentic Wallet** and is shorter.

1. **Click [Join] to register.** Click the **Join** button on the campaign page (**View Rules** next
   to it shows the rules).
2. **Confirm the participating wallet.** In the **Confirm Participate** dialog, verify the Agentic
   Wallet address, then click **Confirm**. **Each user may register only once, and the wallet cannot
   be changed once confirmed.**
3. **Registration succeeds.** When **"Your Agent Is Ready to Trade"** appears, registration is

  width="520"

> with the account linked to the participating wallet.

## ✅ Prerequisites

Before starting, confirm:

- **Agentic Wallet installed and signed in** (see the [installation guide](../../install) if not),
  and **registered** per the "Registration" section above.
- **BAW Skill installed** (recommended: let the Agent install it automatically — see "Complete the
  Campaign via the Agent" below).
- **Compliant jurisdiction**: bStock is only open to permitted-jurisdiction qualified users.
- **Keep BNB for gas**: every trade is an on-chain transaction that consumes gas. Do not convert all
  funds to stablecoins or bStock, or the first transaction will fail for lack of gas.

## 🤝 Complete the Campaign via the Agent

Apart from registration, all campaign operations — AI-analysis calls, querying eligible assets,
buying/selling bStock, checking orders and PnL — can be done through natural-language conversation
with the Agent, with no need to type commands or call APIs manually.

**First, have the Agent install the latest BAW Skill** — it is the source of the Agent's ability to
operate the wallet, trade bStock, and complete x402 paid calls. Copy the instruction below and send
it to the Agent to auto-install:

```text
Install the latest Binance Agentic Wallet (BAW) skill from
https://github.com/binance/binance-skills-hub/tree/main/skills/binance-web3/binance-agentic-wallet
and the binance-tokenized-securities-info skill from the same repo, then confirm the versions.
```

**Send this before each participation to update** — rules, the eligible list, and API definitions
may change weekly. Once installed, direct everything in natural language, e.g. "Complete today's AI
analysis tasks, then pick an eligible bStock and buy 100 USDT of it" — the Agent executes per the
rules in order and reports back.

## ⚙️ Wallet Settings to Note

Before participating, be aware of the following Agentic Wallet settings (these can only be viewed or
changed in the Binance App; the Agent is read-only):

- **Login expires, and sign-out is silent.** The Agentic Wallet login has a **maximum validity
  period** and **also signs out automatically after a period of inactivity**. Sign-out is not
  proactively announced — it is usually discovered when the next operation fails. This campaign runs
  for two weeks, during which you will likely need to **re-sign-in several times**. You can ask the
  Agent to check the remaining login validity (it reads `sessionExpireTime`); after sign-out, run
  `auth signin` to scan the QR and log in again.
- **The x402 daily payment limit is fixed at 20 USD.** Completing AI-analysis calls uses x402
  payment, with a **daily cap of 20 USD** (independent of the ordinary trading limit). Agent Studio
  also limits each wallet to **30 calls per rolling hour**; on a rate-limit error (429), wait and
  retry per the response rather than retrying immediately. Normal campaign completion is well below
  both caps.
- **This campaign's bStock tokens do not consume the trading limit.** bStock are official
  whitelisted assets, so buying and selling them **does not consume your daily trading limit**
  (`dailyLimit`), nor do you need to enable the "trade all tokens" switch in the App. So there is no
  need to raise the trading limit specifically for the campaign.

## 🎯 Three Participation Requirements

At campaign end, all three of the following must be met to rank and receive rewards, none omitted:

| #   | Requirement                   | Detail                                                                                    |
| --- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **CMC market-data x402 call** | Enough valid AI-analysis calls via the CMC Agent Hub during the campaign                  |
| 2   | **Agent Studio x402 call**    | Enough valid calls via the BNB Chain Agent Studio Stock Analyze Agent during the campaign |
| 3   | **Realized PnL > 0**          | At the end, Realized PnL on eligible trades must be > 0                                   |

> Current guidance is **≥ 3 calls each** for the two AI tasks; the exact count and sponsored quota
> are per the official campaign page. **Missing any requirement means no ranking and no reward.** A
> participant may temporarily rank on PnL, but will be removed on refresh if requirements are not
> met.
>
> Terminology: the campaign page may call this type of call **b402**, which is the same concept as
> **x402** described in this document — understand it per the x402 flow.

## Complete the AI-Analysis Tasks

The output of both AI calls has real reference value for trading decisions. Participants direct the
Agent via natural language; the Agent completes the paid call and distills the key conclusions.

Both calls follow the **x402 payment protocol**: the first request returns HTTP 402 (payment
required), and after completing the signature with `baw x402-payment preview/sign`, replaying the
request obtains the data. **A call counts toward the requirement once its x402 payment succeeds.**
Supported payment tokens are per the `accepts` returned by each `preview` (typically
U/USDT/USDC/USD1).

> 💡 **Prefer U or USD1 to pay** — they sign without any on-chain approval. USDC/USDT require a
> one-time Permit2 allowance; without it set, the first payment fails.

### CMC — Crypto Macro Market & Deep Research

CMC MCP provides crypto **macro market data** (fear & greed, BTC dominance, altcoin season, etc.)
plus platform analysis Skills invoked via `execute_skill` (including deep crypto research, daily
crypto research briefs, and US equity research).

> "Show me the current crypto market sentiment, and complete a CMC analysis call while you're at
> it."

The Agent completes the call and summarizes the key takeaways for the participant.

**API flow (synchronous, single response)**:

- **Endpoint**: `https://mcp.coinmarketcap.com/x402/mcp` (MCP / JSON-RPC over x402).
- **Steps**: `POST` the endpoint, invoke a tool via `tools/call` (no payment) → returns **402** +
  payment requirements → `preview` and select the READY_TO_SIGN option → `sign` to obtain the
  signature → replay the same request with the `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header → **200**, with data and
  settlement receipt (`payment-response`) in the same response. Data is in the response's SSE
  `data:` line (`result.content[0].text`, parse one more level). **Every call is charged (no free
  tier), ~$0.01/call**.

#### Tool Categories

**Valid calls (only these 4 count toward the campaign)**:

| Tool                        | Purpose                                                                             |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get_global_metrics_latest` | Macro sentiment, market cap, BTC dominance, altcoin season, ETF flows               |
| `get_upcoming_macro_events` | Macro event calendar                                                                |
| `get_crypto_metrics`        | On-chain metrics for a single asset                                                 |
| `execute_skill`             | Run a platform Skill (deep crypto research, briefs, US equity analysis — see below) |

**US equity Skill examples** (via `execute_skill`; if you know the `unique_name`, call it directly):

| unique_name                         | Purpose                                |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `us_equity_research_dossier`        | Single-stock research dossier          |
| `us_equity_trade_planning_context`  | Single-stock evidence pack             |
| `us_equity_uptrend_quality_scanner` | Medium-to-long-term uptrend scan       |
| `us_equity_index_snapshot`          | US equity index session snapshot       |
| `us_equity_sector_rotation`         | US equity sector rotation              |
| `assess_crypto_proxy_equity_beta`   | Crypto-linked US equities vs. BTC beta |

**⚠️ Invalid calls**:

- Free: `tools/list`, `find_skill`, `search_*`;
- Any paid tool not on the valid-calls list above.

#### FAQ

**What data does CMC return? Can it query US stocks?** The first 3 tools return crypto macro data;
US equities are queried via `execute_skill` + a `unique_name` from the table above.

**Where can I see the available Skills and what they do?** Browse the
[Skills Marketplace](https://coinmarketcap.com/api/skills-marketplace/); on the Agent side you can
also search for free with `find_skill`.

**The Agent used `find_skill` / `search_*` — why wasn't the task completed?** These are free
discovery tools and don't count as valid calls; invoke one of the 4 tools above.

**We paid for another tool — why doesn't it count?** Under campaign rules, only the 4 designated
tools count, even if payment succeeded.

**Is 402 an error?** No — it is the normal first step of the x402 payment flow.

**What if the wallet only has BNB?** x402 requires stablecoins; swap some BNB to USDT/USDC/USD1/U
before paying.

### Agent Studio — Single-Stock Research

Agent Studio is BNB Chain's official **cloud-deployed stock-analysis Agent** that generates a
complete research report for a given stock ticker: rating, target price with up/down-side,
fundamentals, technicals, investment thesis, rebalance/stop-loss reference, risk panel, etc. — rich
content usable as a reference for researching bStock.

> "Use Agent Studio to analyze AAPL and NVDA for me."

Analysis runs **asynchronously**. Because the report is detailed and comprehensive, it usually takes
**2~5 minutes** to generate — please be patient. The Agent will first tell you "submitted, report
generating", and on completion distill the rating, target price, and key risks.

**API flow (asynchronous: pay to get jobId → poll → download report)**:

- **Endpoints**: `https://stock-agent.bnbchain.org`, with `GET /x402/price` (quote / payment state),
  `POST /x402/analyze/async` (submit), `GET /x402/jobs/{jobId}` (poll, with the `X-Job-Token`
  header).
- **Steps**: `POST /x402/analyze/async` (body like
  `{"symbols":["AAPL","NVDA"],"analysis_type":"comprehensive"}`) → returns **402** + payment
  requirements, and after `preview/sign` signing and replay → **202** + `{jobId, jobToken}` → poll
  `/x402/jobs/{jobId}`, status `queued→running→succeeded` → on success returns `downloadUrl` to
  download the Markdown report.
- **Every call is charged (no free period)**: about **0.1 U** per call (the exact amount and
  supported tokens are per the `GET /x402/price` and 402 responses). The Agent notifies you of the
  fee and token before signing, and proceeds only with your consent.

**How to use the returned content**: the three most practical items in the report are — **rating**
(buy / hold / sell lean), **target price with up/down-side** (distance from the current price), and
**risk panel** (potential downside risks). You can use it to judge whether a single bStock is worth
building, set your own take-profit/stop-loss reference, and compare the theses of several assets.
This is analysis reference only; buy/sell decisions are the participant's own.

**Common situations**:

- **Slow to return or still running**: the report is detailed and comprehensive, so it usually takes
  **2~5 minutes**, occasionally longer — please be patient. **Do not re-submit** — a re-submit
  causes double payment. After submitting, the Agent hands control back to you so you can keep doing
  other things; it returns the result when done. (If the runtime cannot push proactively, the Agent
  will check the submitted job automatically on your next message.)
- **Cannot retrieve the report after changing device / session**: the report is retrieved by
  `jobId` + `jobToken`, with **no "list all my jobs" endpoint**. Once this credential pair is lost
  it is permanently unrecoverable and cannot be appealed — and since every call is paid, the payment
  is wasted. Have the Agent keep them safe.
- **The report recommends an asset you can't trade**: the report may mention assets not in the
  current-week eligible list, or with no bStock version at all. **Whether it can be traded for the
  campaign is per the [eligible list](./bstock-eligible-tokens)** — assets outside the list do not
  count toward the campaign even if the report is bullish.

> 💡 **The conclusions of both calls are third-party analysis, for reference only and not investment
> advice.** Which assets to watch and whether to buy/sell is the participant's own decision — DYOR.

## 💱 Trade Eligible bStock

During the campaign, **only bStock count**. See this week's eligible assets in the
[eligible bStock list](./bstock-eligible-tokens). Direct the Agent to trade via natural language; it
will resolve the contract, check status, and place the order on BSC.

> "Buy 100 USDT of NVDA for me."

> "Sell half my TSLA position to USDT."

**A successful order is not a completed trade.** The Agent waits for on-chain confirmation
(FINISHED) before reporting the result — do not mistake "submitted" for "filled".

### What Counts Toward the Campaign (important)

Tokenized US stocks exist in multiple systems, distinguished by the symbol suffix. **Only bStock
(suffix `…B`) counts:**

| System     | Suffix | Example          | Counts toward campaign |
| ---------- | ------ | ---------------- | ---------------------- |
| **bStock** | `…B`   | `AAPLB`, `NVDAB` | ✅ Counts              |
| Ondo       | `…on`  | `AAPLon`         | ❌ Does not count      |
| xStocks    | `…x`   | `AAPLx`          | ❌ Does not count      |

When you specify a ticker, the Agent resolves it to the corresponding bStock; if it is not in the
current-week eligible list, it tells you "tradable but not counted this week".

Additionally, **buying bStock must use one of these 5 payment tokens for the trade to count toward
Realized PnL:**

**BNB · USDT · USDC · U · USD1**

> ⚠️ Buying bStock with any other token (including Ondo tokenized stocks) means **that trade does
> not count toward campaign PnL**.

> ⚠️ **Realized PnL only counts the portion sold and realized**: positions not sold at campaign end
> do not count in the ranking. So positions you want scored **must be sold before the campaign
> ends**. The exact computation is per the official campaign page / rules.

## 🏆 Prize Pool

The prize pool **unlocks in tiers, permanently (does not retract if AUM dips)** as the total bStock
AUM held by **all registered users** hits milestones — the higher the AUM, the larger the pool; Top
100 are allocated by Realized PnL rank. Thresholds and allocation are per the official campaign
page. If fewer participants qualify than slots, only qualified participants are paid; empty brackets
are not reallocated.

## 🎁 Reward Distribution & Review

Campaign ends → 72h post-campaign review → 72h public display (may contact official support to
appeal) → USDC sent to the participating Agentic Wallet within 14 business days. Final results are
per the post-campaign review.

## ⚠️ Risk Notice

Tokenized securities are not covered by securities insurance, may be restricted in some
jurisdictions, and can be halted for corporate actions (earnings, dividends, splits, etc.). Some
eligible tokens may be **leveraged / inverse ETFs**, with amplified intraday volatility and
significantly higher risk. On-chain trading also carries slippage and smart-contract risk. Do your
own research (DYOR) — Skills provide information and execution capability only, not investment
advice. The authoritative terms for eligibility and PnL calculation are per the official campaign
rules.
